description: HURREVAC is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency; NOAA | National Hurricane Center; USACE, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. HURREVAC (short for Hurr icane Evac uation) is a storm tracking and decision support tool for government emergency managers. Program access is restricted to officials in government emergency management. The program is available free-of-charge for eligble registered users. HURREVAC cannot make the evacuation decision for you. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds. Assets: Critical Facilities, People, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
